thread.title: Asian stocks drop as tech pullback, Nissan CEO’s arrest takes toll

author: Dow Jones Newswires
title: Asian stocks drop as tech pullback, Nissan CEO’s arrest takes toll
text:
Asian stock markets fell Tuesday, following tech-led declines on Wall Street.
Japan’s Nikkei NIK, -1.09% was down nearly 1.1%, with electronics and machinery stocks among the biggest decliners. Sony 6758, -3.09% was down 3% while Fanuc 6954, -2.13% and Hitachi 6501, -2.90% both dropped.
But Japan’s auto sector was the most watched following the arrest of Nissan CEO Carlos Ghosn on Monday. Alliance partners Nissan 7201, -5.45% and Mitsubishi 7211, -6.85% slid in early trading, with Nissan at almost 2½-year lows, ending down 5.5%. Rival Toyota 7203, +1.59% benefited, climbing 1.6%.
Hong Kong’s Hang Seng Index HSI, -2.02% fell 2%, with Tencent 0700, -3.30% down 3% and smartphone-component firms AAC 2018, -3.66% and Sunny Optical 2382, -2.38% also falling. Xiaomi 1810, +8.38% jumped 8% after its third-quarter earnings report.
In mainland China, the Shanghai Composite SHCOMP, -2.13% was down 2.1% and the smaller-cap Shenzhen Composite 399106, -2.72% dropped 2.7%. Among large caps, real estate was off some 1% after Monday’s sharp bounce. Financials, which also were strong Monday, pulled back.
A report about another round of production cuts for iPhones weighed on Apple AAPL, -3.96% suppliers in Asia. Taiwan’s Taiex Y9999, -0.86% fell 0.8% as product assembler Hon Hai 2317, -3.27% dropped 3.2% to hit fresh five-year lows and Taiwan Semiconductor 2330, -1.80% declined 1.8%. Korean memory-chip maker SK Hynix 000660, -3.30% slid another 3.3% and Samsung Electronics 005930, -1.95% lost 2% as the Kospi SEU, -0.86% dropped 0.8%.
Australia’s benchmark index XJO, -0.38% was down 0.3%, and New Zealand NZ50GR, -0.83% and Singapore STI, -1.24% posted losses as well.
